source: Document where this dictionary came from (e.g., 'confirmed by PM via session-analysis investigation YYYY-MM-DD; backfilled from frontend code audit')
_INSTRUCTIONS: Replace this with your product's real event dictionary. Each event you want narrated should have an entry. The placeholder entries below show the full schema — copy the shape and fill in your own events. Delete the _INSTRUCTIONS key when done.

<example_session_start_event>.meaning: Describe what triggers this event in your product (e.g., 'OAuth callback step. Fires immediately after user signs in via SSO').

Page Viewed.meaning: Generic page-view event. Often fires alongside more specific page-view events at the same epoch second. Usually safe to skip in narrative if a more specific event fires within 1 second.
skip_if_followed_by: <List your specific page-view events here, e.g. Home Page Viewed, Settings Page Viewed>

page_url.meaning: Which page the user landed on. Path shape often decides the narration.

referrer.meaning: Structured log metadata — not for narrative.

<example_primary_action_event>.meaning: Describe what user action triggers this event (e.g., 'User submitted a chat message / placed an order / opened a record').
<example_primary_action_event>.narrative_template_follow_up: The user submitted a follow-up query: _"{query}"_
<example_primary_action_event>.interpretation_hint: When two narrative templates exist, pick based on the HIGH property (here: is_follow_up). The event's own property wins over heuristics.

query.meaning: Fill the {query} placeholder in the narrative template. Truncation in Mixpanel is a known platform limit, not a UI bug — do not flag it.

is_follow_up.meaning: Decides which narrative_template variant to use.

<example_toast_or_snackbar_event>.meaning: Toast notification. Used across many surfaces.

toast_title.meaning: The user-visible message. Always include verbatim in narrative.

variant.meaning: Maps to emoji: success → ✅, error/destructive → ❌, info → ℹ️.

bug_patterns._INSTRUCTIONS: Each bug pattern is a deterministic detector run after data is pulled. Delete this key in your real file.

filter_cascade.description: Single click on a parent filter selects all sub-items at once. User then has to uncheck them one-by-one.

detector.condition: filter_values arrays shrink monotonically across consecutive events

filter_cascade.narrative_template: ⚠️ BUG DETECTED: The user clicked a single filter, but the system selected all sub-items at once. They had to uncheck them one-by-one over {window_seconds}s to isolate the one they wanted.

repeated_error_toasts.description: Multiple error/destructive toasts for the same user in a single session indicates the product is failing them repeatedly.
repeated_error_toasts.narrative_template: ⚠️ PATTERN: The user hit {count} error toasts in this session — product is failing them repeatedly.

rapid_fire_same_event.description: ≥4 of the same event in <5 seconds — possible UI feedback loop or accidental clicks.
rapid_fire_same_event.narrative_template: ⚠️ PATTERN: {event_name} fired {count} times in {window_seconds}s — UI loop or accidental clicks.

noise_rules._INSTRUCTIONS: Rules for what to collapse or skip during narration.
skip_in_narrative: <list events that are pure render telemetry, e.g. Chart Loaded, Page Render Timing>
